ledger.hypothesis: the node is ELEMENTWISE with an output of exactly 16 doubles -- the arithmetic is nothing, so 100% of the cost is per-access overhead. The nd:: lowering heap-allocates ~20 shared_ptr<vector<double>> Arrays to do 4x4 work; desiredLocal() then re-fetches matrix0/matrix1/parentWorld via findPlug-by-name + MPlug::getValue + MFnMatrixData even though compute() had just pulled all three through the datablock; and nd_gate_mix decomposes a base matrix that its three compile-time-true gates guarantee it will never read. Remove the allocations and the duplicate DG reads and the whole thing collapses onto the DG plumbing floor.
ledger.risk: every step had to be bit-exact, not merely close. The scalar rewrite replicates nd::norm's ascending acc = acc + x*x fold, nd::dot1d's ascending accumulation, nd::cross's operand order, and nd::inv's Gauss-Jordan partial pivot on the augmented 4x8 -- including its `best < 1e-12` singularity test and its `if (f == 0.0) continue` skip -- operation for operation, all in double. No comparison that selects a pivot or a branch was narrowed, loosened, or reordered. The inverse(L) cache is the one place a stale value could ship: it is keyed on memcmp of all 16 raw doubles of L (bitwise, not tolerance), is a per-instance member under a std::mutex rather than a static registry, and caches only the intermediate inverse -- never the node's output -- so a hit can only return exactly what the recompute would have.
ledger.theme: this node is 4x4 scalar math wearing an ndarray costume: replace the nd:: lowering with stack scalars, stop re-reading the three matrix inputs through MPlug when compute() already holds them, and cache inverse(L) on the exact bits of L

ledger.hypothesis: This node is ELEMENTWISE and tiny -- the whole numerical job is 4x4 scalar math on three matrix inputs, and the polySphere/20000-element inputs the bench drives are never read by compute(). A previous porter had already collapsed the nd::Array lowering to stack scalars and cached inverse(L). That left exactly one repeated Maya-API cost in the hot path: MArrayDataBuilder + 16 x addElement() (each an index search/insert) + arrH.set() commit, rebuilding an output array whose shape is a fixed 0..15 and never changes. Replacing it with jumpToArrayElement(0) + next() over the existing elements, guarded by elementCount()==16 and a per-element elementIndex() check with a full builder fallback, removes the builder allocation and the 16 searches without touching a single written value.
ledger.risk: The in-place path depends on the output array already holding exactly logical indices 0..15. Guarded two ways -- elementCount()==16 up front and elementIndex()==i before each write -- and any mismatch falls through to the original builder path, which rewrites all 16 regardless. No arithmetic, no comparison, and no written value changed, so parity is structurally unaffected.
ledger.theme: write the 16 output-array elements in place instead of rebuilding them through an MArrayDataBuilder every tick; the node turned out to be entirely harness-bound, so the change is unmeasurable rather than a win
